ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, individuals with significant control, and authorized signatories against the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the US OFAC SDN list, domestic Canadian enforcement databases, and insolvency or court-record databases. Senior political exposure is assessed in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and FINTRAC guidance, including family members and close associates of domestic and foreign PEPs. Screening is performed at onboarding and thereafter on an ongoing basis; any adverse match requires refusal of the onboarding or immediate filing of a suspicious-transaction report, notwithstanding the low-risk designation of the target fintech software application.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Limited Partnerships Act and the Business Names Act, the proposed name may be expressed in English and/or French and must use Roman-alphabet letters. A non-Roman script name must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet for registration. The name must be distinguishable from every existing registered name in the Ontario Business Registry and must not contain a number name unless permitted by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant must submit a written Name Decision Review request to ServiceOntario within the appeal period stated in the rejection notice, generally not less than 30 days. The request must include the original Name Search Report, the statutory filing reference number, and a memorandum identifying the distinguishing elements of the proposed name. A review officer will issue a written decision. If the administrative review is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal further to the Director under the Business Names Act and the Limited Partnerships Act, and ultimately to the Divisional Court on questions of law or procedure, or may instead file a fresh declaration using an alternate cleared name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this low-risk, license-exempt fintech software entity provided that a street address in Ontario is designated as the registered office and that the virtual-office provider is authorized to accept service of process. A purely virtual mail-forwarding service without a physical registered office address in Ontario is impermissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection is below 10% for a non-licensed SaaS application with no FINTRAC money-services-business status. The probability increases to an estimated 30% to 50% if the entity later triggers FINTRAC reporting obligations, receives regulated deposits, or becomes associated with a concentration of shell-entity registrations at the same registered-office address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.10, ss. 2–5 and 9; Ontario Regulation 11/95 (Limited Partnership Forms); Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, via Ontario Business Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement and no escrow account requirement. The capital contributions are fixed by the limited partnership agreement; contributions may be in cash or property, and services contributed by a limited partner must be carefully structured to preserve limited liability. No pre-funded escrow account is required before filing the Declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the terms of the limited partnership agreement be and are hereby approved, and the proposed capital contribution of the limited partner be accepted in accordance with the subscribed interest. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership be established at the address stated in the Declaration of Limited Partnership and that all statutory notices be received at that office. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the initial general partner, and [Name] as the chief managing officer, with full authority to manage the affairs of the partnership, and [Name] be admitted as the sole limited partner. RESOLVED, that the general partner is authorized to execute the Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership and any ancillary filings with the Ontario Business Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Ontario Business Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through the Ontario Business Registry or an accredited search house. Review the search report to determine whether the proposed limited partnership name is distinguishable from existing corporate, LP, and trademark records. If the name is available, retain the search report for attachment to the Declaration of Limited Partnership and complete any requested name reservation step in the Ontario Business Registry system.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and business description
Identification documents for all general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried as confusingly similar, select a revised distinctive element, obtain an updated NUANS report, and refile the name request. The matter may also be cured by obtaining consent from the conflicting name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, via Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership under sections 2 and 4 of the Limited Partnerships Act. The declaration must state the limited partnership’s name, general nature of business, Ontario principal place of business, full names and addresses of general partners, and the term of the partnership if it is limited. All general partners must execute the declaration. File the completed form online through the Ontario Business Registry and pay the applicable filing fee. The limited partnership comes into existence when the declaration is accepted by the Minister.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement for internal governance and banking purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or queried, correct the stated deficiencies, file a corrected Declaration or Notice of Change through the Ontario Business Registry, and resubmit within the registry service standard. Any ministerial requirement for additional consent or affidavit must be satisfied before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the accepted Declaration of Limited Partnership and the legal identifiers of the general partner, register the limited partnership for a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number. If taxable supplies in a calendar quarter exceed the CRA small-supplier threshold of CAD 30,000, register for GST/HST. If the entity will hire employees, open a payroll deductions account. Maintain the BN registration records in the Ontario limited partnership’s legal name.
required_dossiers: Legal names and addresses of general partners
Description of business as software-related personal wealth analytics and investment tracking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA raises an entity-matching error, verify the legal name and BN start date, correct the submission through Business Registration Online, and contact the CRA Business Window to reconcile the Ontario LP registration with CRA records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Building and Fire Safety Occupancy Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Ontario municipal building department, local municipal fire department, and Electrical Safety Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before leasing physical office space, confirm that municipal zoning permits a software and cloud services office and no industrial manufacturing operation is being carried out. Obtain the landlord’s evidence of compliance with the Ontario Building Code and Ontario Fire Code. If the tenancy creates a new occupancy or requires tenant improvements, apply for the necessary building permit and final occupancy clearance. Complete fire safety inspection, verify exits, extinguishers, alarm systems, and emergency lighting, and ensure any new electrical load is certified by a licensed electrical contractor.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or letter of intent
Space floor plan and occupant load calculation
Fire alarm and extinguisher maintenance records
Electrical Safety Authority certificate if new equipment is installed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If building or fire inspection identifies deficiencies, complete the corrective work, obtain a signed report from a licensed engineer or fire code consultant, and request re-inspection. Resolution may also be sought through the municipal property standards committee where the dispute concerns a notice of violation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development; local municipal building department. No industrial manufacturing license is required for the ISIC 6201 software/cloud activity, but physical office occupancy must comply with municipal zoning and safety requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Occupancy Permit / Fire Safety Compliance Certificate under the Ontario Fire Code and the Building Code Act, 1992

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Part II.0 environmental assessment not triggered; no EIA report required for a software/cloud office activity. Municipal building and fire permits remain applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or significant VOC emission sources. Sanitary and stormwater discharge must comply with the applicable municipal sewer use by-law. Waste electrical and electronic equipment must be handled under Ontario Regulation 103/04 and hazardous waste under Ontario Regulation 347, with no uncontrolled release to air, land, or water.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Ontario Fire Code, O. Reg. 213/07; structural load compliance under the Ontario Building Code; workplace health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1; barrier-free access and workplace accommodation review under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada), Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal; Ontario Ministry of Finance is responsible for Ontario tax rules but the HST component is administered federally by the CRA for Ontario.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-limited partnership intending to make taxable supplies in Canada must: (1) register extra-provincially as a limited partnership under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.14, obtaining an Ontario registration number via the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch; (2) obtain a CRA Business Number by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or using CRA Business Registration Online; (3) open a GST/HST Program Account with the same Business Number; (4) provide proof of the partnership agreement, foreign entity existence, and nominated representative with Canadian or agency address for CRA service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The Ontario limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes under Income Tax Act subsection 96(1), with income and losses flowing through to partners. For GST/HST purposes, however, the partnership is a deemed person under section 272 of the Excise Tax Act and must account for HST when registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada. Elections available are primarily HST administrative elections: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration election under subsection 240(3.1) of the Excise Tax Act; (ii) election to have the partnership use a nominated representative for CRA correspondence; (iii) for non-resident partners, elections under subsection 96(1) only statutory allocation rules apply. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4-18.6 and 247(11) of the Income Tax Act do not provide elective classification; CRA applies domestic classification based on legal form and may disregard foreign check-the-box elections under anti-hybrid provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) administered by the Canada Revenue Agency under the Excise Tax Act; Ontario is a participating province using HST, which combines 5% federal GST and 8% provincial HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000.00: A person making taxable supplies in Canada is required to register for GST/HST if revenue from taxable supplies made in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 in any four consecutive calendar quarters, or at any earlier time if the person carries on a taxable commercial activity in Canada and is not a small supplier. Foreign entities without a Canadian establishment must evaluate whether their software/analytics subscriptions constitute supplies made in Canada based on place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API stamping, or digital signature regime applies to GST/HST invoices in Ontario or federally. CRA accepts electronic invoices in PDF, XML, or EDI format provided the invoice contains the prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act (section 3 of Schedule V? Actually section 169? and section 3 of Regulations? Specified in CRA GST/HST Memorandum 10.9). Participation in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 invoicing is voluntary, not mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rated under section 1 of Schedule VI (Part V) if the goods are exported from Canada by the supplier or recipient under proof of export, with no use in Canada after supply. For offshore financial-software/analytics services: zero-rated under section 7 of Schedule VI, Part V and for intangible personal property (software applications, cloud analytics) under section 10 of Part IV, provided the supply is made to a non-resident, the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST, and the supply is not in respect of, or does not directly suffice for, real property or tangible personal property located in Canada at any time. General anti-avoidance rules and the 'directed to persons in Canada' deeming rule must be reviewed for consumer-facing app subscriptions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A / G13A) filed through CBSA Canada Border Export or documented exemption under the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) / eManifest for physical goods exports
Proof of export: bill of lading, ocean/logistics waybill, CBSA stamp, freight-forwarder certificate, or electronic export record with destination-country customs entry
Commercial invoice and export sales contract specifying the non-resident purchaser and exported software/goods description
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-exchange record or corresponding SWIFT payment evidence showing receipt of export sale consideration from the non-resident counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audit may reopen a zero-rating return within four years of assessment; for fraud or attributable neglect, the limitation period is suspended or extended. If the export documentation is found deficient, the zero-rated supply is reclassified as taxable at 13% HST, and the exporter must remit the uncollected HST plus compound daily interest. Civil penalties under sections 280 and 285 of the Excise Tax Act can reach the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the unreported tax, and 50% in cases of gross negligence. Criminal tax-evasion prosecution under section 327.1 of the Excise Tax Act can lead to fines of up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment term of up to five years for knowingly making false export statements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration; oversight of regulated banking treasury activity is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while cross-border payment monitoring is governed by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for residents and non-residents on both current account and capital account transactions. No exchange-control approval is required to remit dividends, interest, royalties, licence fees, or liquidation proceeds. Repatriation to non-resident investors is executed through Schedule I commercial banks and is subject only to Part XIII withholding tax and applicable treaty relief, not to any central-bank authorization. Non-resident capital can be contributed freely; there is no surrender obligation and no administrative limit on foreign-currency accounts of an Ontario limited partnership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts or SaaS/software subscription proceeds. Exporters and licensed software platforms may retain 100% of foreign-currency revenue on deposit or convert it at bank-driven market rates. Canada has no requirement that proceeds be repatriated within X days, and no central-bank percentage must be exchanged into CAD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Treasury Account
Operating Account and Global Transaction Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury and settlement. An offshore digital EMI is not a clearing member of the Canadian Lynx or ACSS systems and cannot lawfully accept deposits in Canada unless licensed or exempt under the Bank Act. It can function only as an acquisition or service layer, or as a sponsored payment facilitator integrated to a Canadian Schedule I bank. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act, a payment service provider must be registered with the Bank of Canada, but final settlement must occur through a Canadian clearing bank. The Ontario LP should therefore use a domestic Schedule I bank as the principal account and treat the EMI/PSP as an optional front-end collection rail for card/IAP flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for non-resident beneficial owners of an Ontario limited partnership when opening a business account through a Schedule I bank. Most banks mandate an in-branch interview for at least one director or authorized signatory and require notarized/certified copies of the LP registration, partnership agreement, UBO register, and passports. Remote video onboarding is available only for established high-net-worth or fintech clients with a prior Canadian banking relationship, and even then enhanced due diligence includes live identity verification and an economic-substance questionnaire. Bare nominee directors with no operational substance are a material refusal risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity from the limited partnership's pass-through ownership structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership register filed under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, UBO ownership schedule showing all individuals holding 10% or more of the partnership, country-of-residence proof, tax residence certificates, personal identification for each UBO, organizational chart, and a notarized source-of-wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds from volatile digital-asset transactions or unregulated payment channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Exchange or licensed custodian statements, transaction-level ledger evidencing commercial origin, audited financial statements, bank statements from originating jurisdiction, source-of-wealth questionnaire, and an explanation memorandum demonstrating that funds are not derived from prohibited activity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent declared activity of fintech software subscription tracking versus incoming cross-border capital injections or commingling of investor money.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SaaS revenue forecast, merchant settlement statements from Stripe and Apple IAP, subscription agreements, software deployment contracts, segregation policy, inter-company transfer-pricing documentation, and a written treasury policy confirming that escrowed investor funds are never mixed with operating revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person screening hits on non-resident LP investors or counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening exception letter, sanctions risk assessment, Global Affairs Canada and Special Economic Measures Act compliance policy, confirmation of zero transactions with designated persons or sanctioned territories, PEP status disclosure, and an enhanced ongoing monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited physical substance or nominee director arrangement causing the bank to classify the LP as low-residency and high-risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario registered office services agreement, local business license or extra-provincial registration, evidence of director work experience and tax identification, virtual office or lease contract, service invoices to licensed professionals, and an economic-substance narrative tied to the CA_ON software portfolio tracking business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Funds must be transferred only to the LP's designated Schedule I corporate account in the legal name of CA_LP. Inbound CAD wires arrive via SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pain.001 using purpose code 'CAP CONTRIB' and narrative 'Capital injection for software platform development'. If the investor sends USD, the receiving bank executes a spot conversion to CAD and may report an EFT or large cash transaction to FINTRAC if the amount is at least CAD 10,000. Verification requires bank credit confirmation, source-of-funds documentation, LP control agreement, and investor identification records. Third-party or personal-account remittances must be rejected to preserve corporate treasury integrity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD disbursements are cleared through the CPA ACSS for low-value automation and through CPA Lynx RTGS for high-value vendor payments. Cross-border obligations are settled via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers or MT202 COV interbank transfers. Hardware or software licensing settlements may be structured as commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 through scheduled-bank trade desks. Stripe and Apple IAP remittance proceeds are received by ACH/EFT through the merchant acquiring bank and swept to the operating account. Outbound dividends or profit allocations to foreign LP partners are transmitted by MT103 with applicable Part XIII withholding certification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies excluding CAD
Multi-currency notional pooling and treasury sweeps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return for Ontario Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ServiceOntario – Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Company and Personal Property Security Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late grace period; failure to file within the filing window is a contravention of the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act. The Registrar may issue a notice of intention to revoke registration, and after a two-year default the registry may strike the LP from the register. A struck-off LP cannot carry on business in Ontario and must pay all back fees plus court-ordered reinstatement costs to restore legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Income Slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the fiscal year ends on December 31, due no later than March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD$25 per day, minimum CAD$100, capped at CAD$2,500, plus separate late-slip penalties under section 162 of the Income Tax Act; repeated default may trigger CRA audit and compliance orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if LP is a GST/HST registrant and an annual filer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than three months after the partnership's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late remittance interest at the prescribed CRA rate plus 6% per annum; late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid amount, increased by 1 percentage point per full month (maximum 12 months); persistent failure may result in CRA asset garnishment and revocation of GST/HST registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Maintenance of Registered Office / Registered Agent Status (certificate of existence, address confirmation, agent consent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: ServiceOntario (via registered agent or LP solicitor)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the same date as the Annual Return filing, within 60 days after the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect registered address or agent details on the annual return may render official notices invalid, expose the LP to administrative default, and allow ServiceOntario to determine that the LP has abandoned its registered presence in Ontario.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is imposed by the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act. An audit becomes compulsory only when (i) the partnership agreement or a unanimous resolution of partners requires it, (ii) the LP is a publicly traded limited partnership under Canadian securities law, or (iii) the Canada Revenue Agency demands audited financial statements as part of an income tax or GST/HST compliance audit. For a private SaaS/Fintech LP, a compilation or review engagement is normally sufficient unless contractual covenants or investor obligations require a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private LPs. If the LP reports to non-Canadian investors, IFRS is commonly used to align with the parent's reporting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not require a standalone annual UBO report for limited partnerships. All changes to general or limited partners and contribution amounts must be filed immediately as an Amended Declaration with ServiceOntario. For Canadian AML/ATF compliance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the LP must maintain a written beneficial-ownership record, verify all new partners, and refresh the record at least once every 12 months or whenever a relevant transaction or ownership change occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners (full legal names, jurisdictions of residence, contribution details)
Register of Limited Partners (full legal names, capital contributions, profit-sharing percentages, foreign ownership information)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, consent minutes, capital-call records, buy-sell agreements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD $250–$600 (approximately USD $190–$450) per year for Ontario registered office and compliance agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD $4,000–$10,000 (approximately USD $3,000–$7,500) for a full Canadian GAAP/IFRS audit of a SaaS/Fintech LP; if no audit is mandatory, CAD $1,500–$3,000 (USD $1,100–$2,300) for a compilation or review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal/Ontario general corporate rate: 25.0% (15.0% federal + 10.0% Ontario). A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent; the LP itself is not subject to entity-level corporate tax. A corporate partner includes its allocated LP income in Part I taxable income and pays federal and Ontario corporate tax at the applicable combined rate (general or small business).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation partners may claim the federal/Ontario Small Business Deduction reducing the combined effective rate to 12.2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income. Federal SR&ED tax credits and Ontario innovation tax credits are available on qualifying software development costs, but must be claimed by the partner, not by the LP. No statutory tax holiday applies to this fintech business.
